reasons: Covers a flagged case, an allowed case, and a random property check.
Random test runs 500 cases on each run.

terms.meaning: a test that runs many random inputs and checks a rule always holds
a testing library that creates random inputs for property tests

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for share tests
sections.what: Brings in the fraction type, the random test tools, and the share check and split functions.
sections.why: Needed so the tests can run both checks. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: test_float_share_annotation_fires
sections.title: Float share flagged test
sections.what: Checks that a float-typed share argument produces exactly one violation.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the main float rule still fires. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: test_rational_share_annotation_does_not_fire
sections.title: Exact share allowed test
sections.what: Checks that a share written as integer numerator and denominator produces no violations.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the approved pattern is accepted. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: test_random_subdivision_sequences_preserve_exact_total
sections.title: Random split total test
sections.what: Runs many random sequences of splits and checks that the parts still add up to exactly one.
sections.why: Likely reason: proves that exact splitting never loses or gains any part of a share. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Limited to 30 splits per sequence, so very long chains are not covered.

summary: Tests that the share float check flags float share annotations, allows exact fraction shares, and that exact splitting keeps the total at one.
purpose: Proves the share rule works and that the exact split math holds for many random inputs.
why: Likely reason: the random test checks a rule that is hard to cover with a few hand-picked cases. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Runs a float share annotation and expects one violation. Runs an integer numerator and denominator share and expects none. Runs 500 random sequences of splits and checks the parts still sum to exactly one.
inputs: Small Python source examples and random split weights generated by the test tool.
outputs: Pass or fail results for the three tests.
risks: The random test depends on the split function being correct, so a bug there can fail this test in confusing ways.
debug: If the random test fails, read the failing weight list it reports and run the split function by hand on those weights.
